blocks.text: The Cannes Film Festival gets the “Bobycolor” treatment in a collection of close-ups, sequences and offbeat viewpoints by the photographer of Cafoucho. Since 2023, Boby has been roaming the movie-city, sketching portraits of celebrities as well as capturing the backstage of this gathering where all kinds of audiences meet. Working for several newspapers and magazines such as Libération, Les Inrocks and Gala, the photographer delivers vividly colourful images with a delightful vintage touch. His is an invigorating eye that introduces us to a galaxy of characters and situations, tender and zany alike. “You don’t need accreditation to work and take good pictures,” says Boby with a smile. “The whole town takes on the festival’s colours, people let themselves be photographed, they’re well dressed… Visually, it’s an all-you-can-eat buffet!”

Boby shares his encounters, from actresses to unshakeable chess players, by way of the workers bustling behind the scenes and even a Brazilian who is mad about beach football. Following on from his fanzine Croisette 2000 (Fisheye Éditions, 2022), this far more generous new volume brings together images gathered over the last four editions of the Festival. The book comes as a slipcase box that borrows the graphic codes of a VHS tape, a way of paying tribute to a film culture that has nourished the photographer’s eye. Among those you will meet are Virginie Efira, Adèle Exarchopoulos, Monica Bellucci, Ron Howard, Pedro Almodóvar and Woody Harrelson… all while recalling the aesthetic of Tarantino, one of the author’s favourite directors, who also grew up on the VHS of Jurassic Park, which he literally “wore out with his little brother”, as he did the cassette of Miyazaki’s Porco Rosso. “If there were a soundtrack to listen to while flipping through the storyboard that this book amounts to, it would be rock, electro and disco,” the photographer adds. Action!
